title: One occurrence copied into two places
why: Ambiguity must be EXPRESSED. Both successors are equally supported; choosing one and dropping the other silently loses a real finding. Paired with added-file-is-an-evidenced-birth this also fixes where the line falls: Broker/DocCopy.cs is new in revision B, but it is recorded as a COPY of Broker/Doc.cs, so the arrival has a source. A new file with a recorded source is a branch candidate; a new file that is a copy of nothing is a birth. Without that distinction the two cases would be the same shape with opposite answers.

expect.note: each successor takes a FRESH child id recording occ-a1's lineage as parent; letting occ-b1 inherit it outright would elect a winner in the id layer after the outcome refused to

forbid: continued to exactly one of them
a branch recorded without parent_lineage - a child with no parent is a birth wearing the word branched
